rationale: Scaffolded off a VO2 max of 53.4 (LT pace 4:24/km) and a currently light running base (13.5km/week) against a much heavier daily cross-training habit — you train HYROX most days (near-daily indoor cardio plus race-pace rehearsals) alongside running, which is why the real intensity distribution is inverted (16% easy vs an 80% target) and this week's load is running about 2x the rolling norm (ACWR 2.0, 20h of sleep debt, RHR +2.6bpm on baseline). Training_status reads Recovery and the composite readiness band is 'moderate' with an overtraining flag of caution, so Base phase leans on volume and genuinely easy running rather than stacking more intensity on top of the existing cross-training load. A consistent ~3% positive-split habit (pacing ratio 1.027) shows up across recent efforts, so the progressive runs and race-pace blocks through the plan double as pacing-discipline reps, and cadence (currently 155-163spm vs the 170-180 range that usually goes with efficient form) gets deliberate attention via strides and the explicit 172-174spm targets on the Peak-phase speed and VO2max sessions.
tips: Your actual intensity distribution is 16% easy vs an 80% target — the single biggest lever in this plan is running the easy days genuinely easy, not the workout content.

This week's training load is running about 2x your rolling norm with real sleep debt behind it — if a session feels heavy, trim it rather than force it; the week 3 cutback exists to let this settle, not to create the need for one.

You habitually go out ~3% too fast and fade (positive-split ratio 1.027) — every progressive run and race-pace block in this plan is also pacing-discipline practice; run the first third deliberately conservative.

Cadence sits at 155-163spm on recent runs, below the 170-180 range that usually goes with efficient form — lean on the stride sessions and the explicit cadence targets on the Peak-phase speed/VO2max work to nudge it up before race day.

Keep the daily HYROX cross-training volume level, not increasing, through Base — it's already a meaningful share of this week's load spike, and running volume should be the only thing ramping through the block.
